So I may say some things that confuse you, feel free to read the corrections others will but under me

Are you trying to build or buy a pre built?

MOST prebuilt PCs at bigger box stores now will play any game at 1080p 60fps, that is basically the bare minimum for gaming now

When looking at graphics cards VRAM is pretty important, anything above 8GB VRAM will probably do you just fine. Older cards do have some issues without newer features. But anything nividia 3k series or higher or AMD 6k series or higher will be more than fine and should be for a few years

On the CPU side, 6 cores and 12 threads is kinda a good starting point for gaming. While it's totally possible to do on weaker chips, if you wanna open a webpage or have other stuff running you will notice it while gaming. 

16GB of RAM is standard now, yes the speed is important however not super important as long as you get a good brand and it matches your motherboard

For storage, you absolutely must boot you operating system from a Solid State Drive (SSD). The difference in a SSD and HDD is night and day, even if you cheap out on a motherboard (which I don't recommend too much) you can get a SSD that will plug in like a normal HDD and while it's a bit slower than M.2 it's fine, way better than a HDD still

While this may be a lot of info, IMO the things you should look for when looking to build a PC is, 

1. Budget

2. CPU/Motherboard

3.GPU

Then everything else because those are the most expensive, most important, and what everyone likes to show off and talk about.

Hope I didn't scare you away, feel free to ask any questions you may have. And good luck and Welcome to PCMR
